corrected_proposal.title: Trump Said He Instructed DOJ to Terminate Remaining Biden-Era U.S. Attorneys
corrected_proposal.description_short: Reuters reported that Trump instructed DOJ to terminate remaining Biden-era U.S. attorneys; implementation of all terminations is not established.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: On February 18, 2025, Donald Trump said he had instructed the Justice Department to terminate all remaining U.S. attorneys appointed under Joe Biden, Reuters reported. Reuters also described earlier notices to several attorneys and other departures. The report documents Trump’s instruction, not completion of a nationwide purge or installation of loyalist replacements.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On February 18, 2025, President Donald Trump said he had instructed the Justice Department to terminate all remaining U.S. attorneys appointed during Joe Biden’s administration, according to Reuters. Trump described the department as politicized and called for it to “clean house.” Reuters reported that the White House had sent termination notices the prior week to several Biden-appointed U.S. attorneys. Other attorneys announced departures, while some had already left government. The report therefore supports a public instruction directed at the remaining Biden-era attorneys and separate notices or departures involving some prosecutors. It does not establish that every U.S. attorney was removed, that all 93 were fired on January 20, or that loyalist replacements were installed by dawn. The article also does not show that the instruction bypassed Senate confirmation or that a court ruled it unlawful. The original entry’s first-night purge and replacement claims should not be retained. The event is the reported February instruction; its implementation and any effects remain unresolved.

source_fact_map.fact: Trump said on February 18, 2025, that he instructed DOJ to terminate remaining Biden-era U.S. attorneys.

insight_facts: A reported instruction was made on February 18, 2025; implementation of all removals is not established.

impact_proposal.confidence_reason: Reuters reports a public instruction; completion and effects remain unverified.
impact_proposal.rationale: The instruction targeted remaining Biden-era U.S. attorneys across the federal system, supporting national reach and limited institutional pressure. The reviewed reporting establishes no realized harm, procedural bypass, private benefit, or durable effect.
impact_proposal.basis: Reuters report of Trump’s February 18 instruction and described notices/departures.
impact_proposal.notes: Editorial estimate under impact-v2; instruction occurred, downstream implementation is not established.
